props.statement: The catalysts may be known catalysts (not favouring methane) that both combine the gases and are sufficiently basic to form methanol directly; or mixtures in which some initiate the combination and others, strongly basic, transform the initial products into methanol; or the gases may pass successively over combining catalysts and basic catalysts.

props.note: cited from the prior art (British patent specification of Badische Anilin & Soda Fabrik No. 20488 of 1913)
props.statement: Mixtures of carbon monoxide and hydrogen in which carbon monoxide largely preponderates give, at high temperature and pressure, hydrocarbons with a series of oxygenated aliphatic products; the process is of little commercial value because many products are formed in small amounts and are hard to separate.

props.note: cited from the prior art; the patent argues against it
props.statement: Later researches (Patart and others) prescribed, as the main modification, a substantial excess of hydrogen, stated to give essentially methanol.

props.name: combination probably via formaldehyde; basic catalyst forms methanol from it

evidence.quote: which are capable of initiating combination of the hydrogen and carbon monoxide, proba- bly to form formaldehyde, and owing to their having at the same time a basic character, are capable of forming methyl alcohol, probably

evidence.note: printed as 'splitting off carbon monoxide from formaldehyde'
evidence.quote: by splitting off.carbon monoxide from form- aldehyde, or that one employs catalysts

props.statement: The catalysts probably initiate the combination of hydrogen and carbon monoxide to formaldehyde and, owing to their basic character, form methyl alcohol from it, probably by 'splitting off carbon monoxide from formaldehyde' (as printed).
